title: Builder
summary: Assemble a complex object step by step; keep the product immutable at the end.

parts.rule: Builder accumulates pieces through chained steps, then build produces the product. Use it when constructors would need many optional parameters or when construction order has constraints. Prefer immutable products after build so half-built objects cannot leak.
parts.why: Telescoping constructors with six positional arguments are unreadable and easy to swap. Builders name each part at the call site. Misuse leaves long-lived mutable builders as the API instead of the product.

body:
Rule. Builder accumulates pieces through chained steps, then build produces the product. Use it when constructors would need many optional parameters or when construction order has constraints. Prefer immutable products after build so half-built objects cannot leak.

Why it matters. Telescoping constructors with six positional arguments are unreadable and easy to swap. Builders name each part at the call site. Misuse leaves long-lived mutable builders as the API instead of the product.

Worked example. QueryBuilder selects id and name, from users, where active is true, orderBy name, limit 10, then build returns an immutable Query holding SQL text and bound params. Calling build twice without changes yields equivalent queries. An invalid sequence such as where without from should throw at build time. HTTP request builder sets url, header, body, timeout, then build returns Request. Contrast that with eight constructor overloads for every optional header combination. When to use. Use builders for queries, complex config objects, test data fixtures, and immutable messages with many fields. Use them when readability of construction matters in call sites.

When to refuse. Refuse a builder for three required fields with no options. Refuse leaving builders as the long-lived mutable API instead of the product. Refuse build succeeding in blatantly invalid states. Refuse a builder when a simple options struct plus one constructor is clearer.
